name: Morus

project_scope.note: Genus comparison only; no species installation or native-range certification.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Check alternate leaves and milky latex, then examine the UNDERSIDE of several mature leaves at 10×. Verify buds and female flower clusters.
shared_traits: Woody deciduous mulberries with alternate simple, toothed or lobed leaves and stipules.
Minute unisexual flowers in compact clusters; female clusters mature into elongated fleshy MULTIPLE fruits.
Leaves vary in lobing, especially on juvenile or sprout growth.

species_comparison_matrix.Morus alba: Generally glabrous between veins, with hairs mainly on veins or at vein axils.
species_comparison_matrix.Morus microphylla: Short stiff hairs on both leaf faces; small rough leaves.
species_comparison_matrix.Morus rubra: Soft hairs across lower blade, including between veins; upper face commonly rough.

species_comparison_matrix.Morus alba: Usually rounded buds; often less strongly dark-edged scales.
species_comparison_matrix.Morus microphylla: Slender, often zigzag and hairy young twigs; bud detail needs local review.
species_comparison_matrix.Morus rubra: Often flattened oblique buds with dark-edged scales.

species_comparison_matrix.character: Pistillate style branches (supporting; regional validation needed)

species_comparison_matrix.Morus alba: Often 1–3 cm; can be white or dark.
species_comparison_matrix.Morus microphylla: Often around 1–1.5 cm, dark at maturity.
species_comparison_matrix.Morus rubra: Often around 2–3 cm, dark at maturity.

field_steps: Check milky latex and alternate leaves; inspect the compact multiple fruit if present.
Compare fully expanded leaf undersides at 10×: hairs between veins, not merely on veins.
Measure several mature leaves; compare bud shape and twig hairs.
Use flowering/fruit characters for confirmation; mark ambiguous or hybrid-like specimens Morus sp.
overlap_cautions: Leaf lobing and fruit color are unreliable species separators.
M. alba and M. rubra hybridize; intermediate hairs and buds need review.
M. microphylla can overlap drought-stressed small-leaved forms; never use size alone.
M. alba is an introduced comparison, not a confirmed target-zone native.

2026-10-12 scientific review: Arizona Extension describes M. microphylla short stiff hairs on both leaf faces, but a broader Morus key places underside pubescence mainly along veins; do not present one hair-distribution pattern as universal. Confirm local voucher specimens.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.separator: Huge globose multiple fruit versus elongated Morus fruit.
Single drupes, not mulberry multiple fruits; lack characteristic milky latex.
Winged dry samaras rather than fleshy multiple fruit.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Matched 10× macros of all three species, annotate hairs between veins versus vein-only.
Three mature leaves per species with ruler, both surfaces.
Matched dormant bud and leaf-scar macros showing scale edges.
Dissected flowers of M. alba and M. rubra with 1-mm scale.
Measured mature infructescences; close-up of individual fruit units and Maclura comparison.

handoffs.question: Verify Texas M. microphylla versus M. rubra hair/size limits and alba × rubra hybrids; check regional style-length key.
All three source-pool species absent from manifest; verify accepted concepts and preserve range labels before installing.
Acquire matched underside, bud and flower macros; no generic photo substitutes.
